prompt: Let $A$ be a set and $R\subseteq A\times A$ a binary relation on $A$. For $x,y\in A$, write $R(x,y)$ for $(x,y)\in R$. What does it mean for $R$ to fail reflexivity?

answers.explanation: Negating a universal statement gives one missing self-loop; loops elsewhere may still be present.
No element has a self-loop; pairs of different elements are unrestricted. This is not the negation of reflexivity.
Every element has a self-loop; pairs of different elements are unrestricted. This is not the negation of reflexivity.
Every related pair has its reverse; loops are allowed but not required. This is not the negation of reflexivity.
Only one element needs to relate to itself. This is not the negation of reflexivity.
No ordered pair is present, including between distinct elements. This is not the negation of reflexivity.
Every related pair has no reverse. Taking the two elements equal also forbids loops. This is not the negation of reflexivity.
Some related pair lacks its reverse; this is an existential violation. This is not the negation of reflexivity.
Every related pair is diagonal; some or all loops may be missing. This is not the negation of reflexivity.
One related pair suffices; the other elements may be isolated. This is not the negation of reflexivity.
